sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: forecast-versus-outcome amounts across two documents, with the forecast amount printed nowhere and a look-alike measure (growth rates) in the same sentence as the dollar gap; target medium (the lower of the two tiers the user named open; the page showed Hard 0/5 · Medium 0/1 · Easy 0/0, and runs on 2026-10-14 started at the High level). Quick test: the sketch survived (user, 2026-10-14, "all survived": i01, i02 and i03). Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 gives the gaps ($15.3b tax, $3.2b non-tax) and names the forecast (2024-25 Budget); Doc 1 Table 3.1 gives the 2024-25 outcomes (657.8, 59.1). Forecast amounts 642.5 and 55.9 (calculated); excesses 2.38% and 5.72%; the larger, 5.7%.
- Universe: two named heads (tax receipts, non-tax receipts). Total receipts (18.5 / 698.5 = 2.6%) is not one of them; payments fell short of no forecast in the same sense ($0.2b over) and are not asked.
- Necessity: D01 is the only source of 2024-25 receipts outcomes (searched "657.8", "59.1", "717.0", "non-tax receipts", "tax receipts" in all ten documents; D04 gives 2023-24 shares of GDP only, D06 is all levels of government by quarter). D03 is the only source of a 2024-25 forecast or forecast gap (searched "forecast", "2024–25 Budget"; D04 gives a preliminary 2024-25 deficit only). Delete-and-guess: without D01 a solver has growth rates only -> 3.3% (tax) or no level; without D03 there is no forecast -> unanswerable; closed book needs four obscure figures -> not reachable.
- Selected-lever checks: Look-alike measure. Wrong routes recomputed: growth gaps 3.9 - 0.6 = 3.3 points (tax) against 7.1 - 4.4 = 2.7 (non-tax), or ratios 1.039/1.006 - 1 = 3.28% and 1.071/1.044 - 1 = 2.59%: both rank tax first and give 3.3%. Gaps over outcomes: 15.3/657.8 = 2.33%, 3.2/59.1 = 5.41% -> 5.4%. Wrong Table 3.1 block (2025-26: 699.5, 60.2): 15.3/684.2 = 2.24%, 3.2/57.0 = 5.61% -> 5.6%. Not a which-items question; the look-alike (tax receipts' larger growth gap) is named in Step 9.
- Targeted failure modes: one declared, the lazy default: Look-alike measure / Takes the wrong line item, wrong answer 3.3% (recomputed above). Not declared (predicted only): gaps over outcomes (5.4%), wrong column (5.6%).
- Calculation verification: script scratchpad/calc1.py (2026-10-14): 657.8 - 15.3 = 642.5; 59.1 - 3.2 = 55.9; 15.3/642.5 = 0.023813; 3.2/55.9 = 0.057245 -> 5.7% at one decimal. Consistency: 642.5 + 55.9 = 698.4 against total receipts forecast 717.0 - 18.5 = 698.5 (rounding); UCB forecast -10.0 - 18.3 = -28.3.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints "642.5", "55.9", "5.7" or "2.4" with this meaning (searched); D01 line 744's "$3.2 billion over the five years to 2029–30" (non-tax parameter variations since MYEFO) and line 1475's "5.7 per cent at MYEFO" (child care growth) are look-alike strings with other meanings. Shortest route found: Doc 3's two gap sentences, Doc 1's 2024-25 block, two subtractions, two divisions.
- Precision/readings: inputs printed to $0.1b, so exact inputs could give 5.63-5.82% for non-tax; every solver works from the printed 3.2 and 59.1 (5.72%). Readings still possible: growth gaps (3.3%), gaps over outcomes (5.4%), wrong column (5.6%); the words "exceeded the amounts ... forecast" and "exceeded those forecasts" (amounts) and the standard sense of "exceeded by x%" (relative to the forecast) reject them; the form's Checks and the run will show whether solvers take them.

sections.question: For the 2024-25 financial year, the Australian Government's tax receipts and its non-tax receipts both exceeded the amounts the 2024-25 Budget had forecast. What is the larger of the two percentages by which they exceeded those forecasts, to one decimal place?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, Fiscal forecasting performance, Tax receipts): tax receipts grew 3.9 per cent in 2024-25 against 0.6 per cent forecast at the 2024-25 Budget, and were $15.3 billion higher than forecast.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 3, Non-tax receipts): non-tax receipts grew 7.1 per cent against 4.4 per cent forecast at the same Budget, and were $3.2 billion higher than forecast.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 1 and Doc 3, Table 3.1 budget aggregates, 2024-25 Actual column): tax receipts were $657.8 billion and non-tax receipts $59.1 billion. Table 3.1 prints each year's column as a separate block; this is the 2024-25 Actual block because its underlying cash balance is -10.0 ($ billion), -0.4 per cent of GDP, the 2024-25 deficit Doc 3 reports, and its gross debt of 928.6 ($ billion) is the figure the balance sheet table prints under "Actual 2024-25".
Step 4. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): forecast tax receipts = 657.8 - 15.3 = 642.5 ($ billion).
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): forecast non-tax receipts = 59.1 - 3.2 = 55.9 ($ billion).
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): tax receipts' excess over their forecast = 15.3 / 642.5 = 2.4%.
Step 7. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): non-tax receipts' excess over their forecast = 3.2 / 55.9 = 5.7%.
Step 8. Final answer (Doc 1 and Doc 3): the larger of 2.4% and 5.7% is 5.7%, for non-tax receipts.
Step 9. Look-alike measure (Doc 1 and Doc 3): the growth rates in Steps 1 and 2 are not gaps between amounts, because each forecast grew from the Budget's estimate of the year before, which the outcome for that year revised. Read as gaps they rank tax receipts first: 3.9 - 0.6 = 3.3 percentage points, more than non-tax receipts' 7.1 less 4.4. That decoy answer, 3.3 for tax receipts, is wrong; the dollar gaps over the forecast amounts give 5.7%.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Look-alike measure: Doc 3 prints each 2024-25 forecast miss as growth rates beside dollar gaps. Comparing growth gaps (tax 3.9 against 0.6 per cent) picks tax receipts, 3.3%. The forecasts grew from a different prior-year base, so only gaps over forecast amounts (Doc 1 outcomes) give 5.7%.
